newsitem.title: UK: UK's SIB moves to strengthen compensation scheme.
newsitem.headline: UK's SIB moves to strengthen compensation scheme.

text.p: Britain's Securities and Investments Board on Thursday issued a consultative paper on proposals to strengthen the financial position of the Investors Compensation Scheme (ICS).
The Scheme enables investors to claim compensation of up to 48,000 stg for loss of money or investments due to the negligence or fraud of failed UK investment firms.

SIB said its main proposal was an amendment to the rules so that the ICS can levy in advance to cover likely compensation pay-outs for expected defaults. It also plans to adopt "a more prudent approach" to estimating the likely costs of defaults.

The SIB said it was also airing, but not proposing, the idea that a reserve fund could be set up for the ICS to be drawn on if its normal sources, the member firms of its constituents such as the Personal Investment Authority and Investment Management Regulatory Organisation, dried up.
